title: debounce() gains a leading option and stops leaking timers

notes.what: debounce(fn, wait, {leading}) now calls fn immediately on the first call in a burst when leading is true, then suppresses calls until wait ms of silence. The returned function gets a cancel() method that clears the pending timer.
notes.why: The search box needed the first keystroke to fire instantly for perceived speed, and unmounted components kept firing stale timers because there was no way to cancel.
notes.edge: With leading true and a single call, fn runs once and never again at the trailing edge, so the trailing call is skipped when nothing happened during the wait. Calling cancel() twice is a no-op. wait of 0 still defers to the next tick in trailing mode.
notes.risk: Existing callers get identical trailing behaviour since leading defaults to false. The timer handle is kept in a closure, so each debounced function holds one timer at most; React effects must call cancel() in cleanup.
notes.test: Fake timers in the unit test: assert one call at t=0 with leading, none during the burst, one trailing call without leading, and that cancel() prevents the trailing call.
